title: Potato Salad with Light Italian Dressing

content.title: About
content.content: Potato salad with light Italian dressing is made from boiled potatoes, fresh vegetables (tomatoes, cucumbers, onion), herbs and a dressing based on olive oil, vinegar, lemon juice, oregano and basil. The dish has a gentle flavor, a light tang and the aroma of Mediterranean herbs.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The Italian dressing makes the salad lower in calories compared with traditional mayonnaise‑based versions.
Potatoes retain most of their vitamin C when they are not overcooked.
In Italy such salads are traditionally served in summer when vegetables are at their peak flavor.
Adding fresh basil boosts the antioxidant properties of the dressing.
The salad can be prepared ahead, but the dressing is best added just before serving to keep the potatoes from becoming mushy.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Potatoes provide slow‑release energy, helping to maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and enhances iron absorption from plant foods.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: The light Italian dressing is mainly monounsaturated fats from olive oil, which are heart‑friendly.

items.title: Antioxidants from herbs
items.content: Oregano and basil contain polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Fiber from vegetables
items.content: Tomatoes, cucumbers and herbs add dietary fiber, supporting digestion.

items.title: Olive oil allergy
items.content: Some individuals may react to olive oil or the herbs used in the dressing.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Excess salt in the dressing can raise blood pressure.

items.title: Bacterial growth
items.content: If the salad sits at room temperature for more than 2 hours, the risk of bacterial contamination increases.

items.title: Starch texture
items.content: Hot potatoes that are not cooled properly can become gummy, affecting the salad’s texture.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled as a side dish or light main course. It works well in sandwiches, as a wrap filling, or alongside fish and poultry. Garnish with fresh herbs and a squeeze of lemon juice before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, keep the dressing separate to prevent the potatoes from becoming soggy.
